subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: Acme Health discovery
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up / Next steps from today's discovery call (Dedicated sizing)

Thanks again for the time today, Sam — good first discussion. Quick recap and a few clarifying Qs so we can put together a sizing proposal and cost estimate for Dedicated capacity (with VPC peering):

- Primary ask: Real-time clinical assistant integrated into clinician UI (no PHI persisted outside of VPC).
- Preferred deployment: leaning toward Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) with VPC peering; you flagged potential interest in Fully Private (on-prem) if required for audit.
- Goals we captured on the call:
  • Average steady-state TPS: ~50 requests/sec
  • Peak TPS: ~120 requests/sec (short bursts during morning rounds)
  • Average token mix: ~120 prompt tokens / ~40 completion tokens (avg ~160 tokens per request)
  • Target P95 latency for 512-token outputs: <= 400ms
  • SLA expectations: business-critical, need 99.9% uptime and incident routing to your on-call

Questions for sizing:
1) Can you confirm average tokens per request (prompt vs completion) and if you expect many long-context prompts (>2k tokens)?
2) Are you planning persistent sessions per patient that reuse KV cache or mostly stateless requests?
3) Any hard preferences on GPU class (H100 vs A100) or must we size for both options in the proposal?

Next steps: If you can confirm the three items above I'll loop in Rafael (solutions engineering) and we'll produce a 1-page estimate + node count with A100/H100 options and suggested autoscale policy. I’ve attached a short sizing worksheet — please fill the highlighted cells if convenient.

Attachment: dedicated_sizing_acme_health.xlsx (worksheet)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks, Marissa — quick clarifications / extra context from our infra team: 

- Token shapes: ~85% of requests are short (<=200 tokens total), ~15% are longer (400-1,200 tokens) for weekly discharge notes. Average still ~160 tokens/request but tail matters for latency.
- Session state: clinicians often have short-lived sessions (stateless) but some workflows will reuse context within a visit (we expect 10-15% cache reuse).
- Compliance note: HIPAA + SOC 2 Type II required; VPC peering is required for the Dedicated plan and we'll want TLS + customer-managed KMS.
- Preferred GPU: infra leans H100 for top-end perf, but A100 is acceptable if cost benefits are substantial. Please size for both.
- Budget: early-stage estimate target is <$XXk/month but we know trade-offs exist — exact number TBD after your sizing.

Can we schedule a technical deep-dive Thurs or Fri? Priya (cc'd) will own procurement coordination.

Sam

Appreciate the details, Sam — that helps a lot. Rafael, looping you in to propose an initial capacity plan and banded estimates for A100 vs H100 (and a short note on autoscale + cache configs). Rafael — highlights from Acme's profile: avg 50 rps steady, 120 rps peak, ~160 tokens/req avg, ~10-15% cache reuse, ~60 concurrent sessions at peak, HIPAA+SOC2 requirement, VPC peering needed.

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up / Next steps from today's discovery call (Dedicated sizing)

Hi Sam / Priya — Rafael from Solutions Engineering here. Quick technical notes after reviewing the worksheet and your numbers. I put together a short initial estimate (attached) — high level below: 

Assumptions from your inputs: avg 50 rps steady, 120 rps peak bursts (~10–15m), avg 160 tokens/req, 10% requests reuse KV cache. Target P95 latency <= 400ms for 512-token outputs.

Estimate (generation workloads only):
- H100 (80GB) option: ~4x H100 GPUs required to meet 120 rps peak with <400ms P95, assuming continuous batching and moderate concurrency (64). This includes ~20–30% headroom for burst smoothing and autoscale buffer.
- A100 (80GB) option: ~6x A100 GPUs to achieve similar latency targets (higher token/sec cost).

Notes / tuning knobs:
- Batching + token-based batching will be critical: effective tokens/sec at peak is ~19.2k tokens/sec (120 rps * 160 tokens).
- KV cache reuse (10%) reduces load by ~10% on average; session affinity will help.
- Autoscale recommendation: base pool to cover steady 50 rps (1–2 GPUs depending on model variant) and scale up by node increments when sustained >70 rps for >30s; allow scheduled scaling for morning rounds.
- If long-tail 1–5% of requests hit >1k tokens frequently, we recommend a small pool of high-memory nodes (H100) dedicated to long-context jobs to avoid throttling short requests.

Next steps I can take now: attach the PDF estimate and a short A/B cost table for H100 vs A100, plus a proposed rollout: canary (1 GPU), regional expansion, then full capacity. I’m happy to run the technical deep-dive Thu 3/12 10:30 PT.

Attachment: initial_capacity_estimate_acme.pdf

If that plan looks good Marissa, I’ll prepare an engineer-facing runbook for the deep-dive and a draft service scope for the Dedicated contract (VPC peering, KMS, SOC2 evidence bundle).

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
